chapters.title: THE THINGS I'LL NEVER LET YOU FORGET

chapter_1.title: WHO ARE YOU?
content: You are someone I keep discovering, even after all these years.
There are so many little things about you that I notice.
Some of them are funny. Some of them drive me crazy.
And some of them make me wonder how I got so lucky.
But if I had to describe you in one word, I don't think I could.
Because you are not just one thing.
You are my best friend, my safest place, my favourite person, and the person I want beside me.
And maybe that's what this whole movie is really about.
Me trying to show you the person I see when I look at you.

chapter_2.title: THE LITTLE THINGS
content: I don't think you even realise how many little things about you I notice.
Like the way you eat green chutney.
You don't even need food sometimes. Just give you a bowl of green chutney and you're happy.
And if I take the bowl away, you literally drag it back.
Then there's your face when you dislike someone. You don't even have to say anything. Your face says everything.
And when we go out to eat, three or four spoons later, you're suddenly completely full.
Then comes the whole performance — leaning back, going 'ooh, ah', trying to open the first button of your shirt and showing me how full you are.
You absolutely love sleeping. Sometimes I genuinely feel you love sleep more than you love me.
And then there's your English.
You're actually amazing at speaking English, and somehow your accent makes you sound like a foreigner.
I just wish you weren't so shy about speaking it in front of other people.
When we walk together, you sometimes push your hand backwards so I can hold it.
You probably don't even notice that you do it.
And before every photograph, you fix your hair.
Then you ask me to take three more. Then four. Then five.
You are ridiculously talented, but somehow you keep thinking you're less than everyone else.
That is one thing about you I really wish I could change.
Because I wish you could see yourself the way I see you.

chapter_3.title: YOUR FACE, YOUR HEART
content: I love your face.
I love your eyes.
And your eyelashes... I don't think you even know how beautiful they are.
Sometimes on our video calls, I'm not even listening to what you're saying. I'm just looking at your eyelashes.
Then there's your little, poky nose.
It's so small and cute that every time I see you, I feel like kissing it.
And your lips... honestly, I don't understand how they are that soft naturally.
But here's the thing.
As beautiful as you are on the outside, that's not what made me fall in love with you.
I fell in love with your heart.
You have one of the purest hearts I've ever known.
You are kind. You are genuine. You are transparent. You stand up for what you believe in.
After a long, exhausting day, when I come back to you, I find so much sincerity and softness.
You're a gem in a world that can sometimes feel very muddy.
Like a lotus in a muddy pond.
So yes, I find you incredibly attractive.
But I didn't fall in love with your face.
I fell in love with your heart.
Your soul.
You yourself.
And to me, my love, you are the most charming and beautiful man I have ever met.

chapter_4.title: HOW WE BECAME US
content: We met on the very first day of our online MSc Physics class.
And honestly, I don't think you had the best first impression of me.
My first WhatsApp message wasn't exactly the warmest introduction.
I didn't ask your name. I didn't ask how you were.
I just started asking you questions about an old friend.
And you basically thought, 'Who is this girl?'
Then I started seeing your WhatsApp statuses — mostly you cooking different things.
And somehow, food became the beginning of our friendship.
We became friends.
Then our offline classes started after summer vacation.
And somewhere along the way, I realised I didn't just like talking to you.
I liked you.
We were best friends for more than a year before those feelings slowly became something more.
Then came our St. Xavier's fest.
Two days. Two nights. So much time together.
And somewhere in those two days, something changed.
Friends became lovers.
One of the funniest memories we still have is that terrible lunch at Royal China.
But one of the moments when I knew you were my person was much quieter.
You wrote me a poem on my first birthday.
You cooked for me.
And whenever I was busy, you would simply say, 'It's okay. You do your work. We'll talk later.'
You never made me feel guilty for having a life.
You made me feel safe.
You made me feel seen.
You made me feel heard.
You respected my choices and my consent.
And I think respect was one of the first things that made me realise that you were my person.
Being with you has changed me too.
I've become more patient, more empathetic, more forgiving and calmer.
And after everything we've been through, the one thing I never want us to lose is that safe space we give each other.
That closeness.
That respect.
That feeling of being home with each other.

chapter_5.title: YOU, THROUGH MY EYES
content: There are things about you that I don't think you realise.
You're one of the most intelligent people I've ever met.
And you're genuinely funny.
Your sarcasm and your humour are top-notch.
The funny thing is, not everyone gets it.
You also understand your surroundings incredibly well.
Sometimes people might think you don't understand something.
But you do.
You notice more than people realise.
Sometimes I feel like you understand me better than I understand myself.
You read me.
You know when something is wrong even when I don't say it.
And something I admire enormously about you is the way you treat equality.
You love cooking. You cook for your mother. You cook for your family.
You don't believe that certain roles belong to certain genders.
That is one of the things that makes you a true modern gentleman to me.
And even after four years together, you still make respect a priority.
You value emotions.
You value emotional availability.
You make space for feelings.
But more than anything, I wish you could see yourself the way I see you.
You have this strange habit of underestimating yourself.
You don't realise how much you bring into people's lives.
You don't realise how much softness there is inside you.
You don't realise how much goodness there is in you.
If I could give you one thing, it would be my eyes for one day.
Just so you could see yourself the way I see you.

chapter_6.title: DISTANCE
content: Almost a year ago, our lives started moving in two different directions.
I moved to Mumbai for my higher studies.
You stayed in Kolkata for your research and your studies.
And suddenly, two cities became part of our relationship.
The hardest part of being apart isn't actually the distance.
It's the goodbye.
We go out. We watch a movie. We have lunch. We spend the day together.
And then suddenly, it's time for the metro.
You go one way.
I go another.
And before that happens, I get one last hug.
I get to feel your perfume, your breath, your warmth.
And then I have to let you go.
Our video calls are honestly quite funny.
Half the time the network doesn't work.
I can't hear you. You can't hear me.
And then suddenly you say, 'Oh, the network issue again.'
But somehow, even through all of that, we're still there for each other.
I went to Kolkata during Durga Puja just to see you.
And after I moved to IIT Bombay, I still remember that first random call.
Just a simple, 'Hi. How are you?'
Nothing dramatic.
But it meant everything.
When I'm having a terrible day, you don't always try to fix it.
You just stay.
And that's enough.
You remember the things that hurt me.
You remember the people who hurt me.
Even when I've forgiven someone, you remember what they did to me.
That's one of the ways I know how deeply you care.
Months can pass.
And when I finally see you again, you're still the same charming person.
Distance hasn't changed you.
It hasn't changed us.
If anything, distance has taught me one thing.
Love doesn't decrease with distance.
It increases.
Exponentially.

chapter_7.title: THE ARCHIVE
content: There are so many things I remember about us.
Not because they were extraordinary.
Just because they were ours.
JW Marriott is one of the happiest memories I have with you.
It was just a beautiful experience. The kind of day I wish I could replay.
Then there are the stupid little memories.
Like our phone calls where neither of us can hear the other because the network is terrible.
And then you suddenly say, 'Oh, the network issue again.'
I don't know why, but that still makes me laugh.
One of the most romantic memories I have is you whispering and singing 'Nishirat Bakhacha Takashi' into my ears in our astrophysics laboratory.
There was a full moon outside.
And somehow that moment has stayed with me.
Then you sang the same song again on our date to Romania Cafe.
Some memories are about places.
Dada Boudir Biryani in Barrackpore will always be one of ours.
We've gone there so many times that it feels like our place.
Then there was Marble Palace and lunch at Bawarchi.
Another completely ordinary day that I remember for no particular reason.
You were wearing a white shirt and jeans.
Your hair was messy.
You hadn't even shaved.
And somehow I thought you looked incredibly attractive.
I was lying on the college bench with my head on your lap.
Nothing extraordinary happened.
But I remember that day.
I remember your face.
I remember how it felt to simply be there with you.
Then there are our songs.
Hum Tere Pyaar Mein Sara Aalam.
Tere Paas Mein.
And the movies that remind me of us.
Edward and Bella.
Rose and Jack.
Shyam Singha Roy.
And that photograph from Victoria Memorial that I absolutely love and you absolutely hate.
You cringe every time you see it.
I still love it.
And then there are the moments when you cook for me or surprise me.
Those are the memories nobody else would understand in quite the same way.
Funny thing is, I don't think my favourite memories are the big ones.
They're the tiny moments that nobody else would remember.
But I do.
Because they happened with you.

chapter_8.title: THE LIFE WE'RE BUILDING
content: I don't really know what our life will look like ten years from now.
But I know who I want to be there.
You.
When I imagine our future, I imagine us married.
But not just husband and wife because that's what the world calls it.
I imagine us still being us.
Still best friends.
Still choosing each other.
Sometimes I imagine Paris.
Sometimes I imagine Venice.
Maybe one day we'll actually wake up there.
I imagine ordinary mornings more than anything else.
I wake up before you.
I work out. I shower. I make coffee.
You wake up a little later.
And before I leave for work, you give me a forehead kiss.
That's the kind of future I want.
I want us to be a team.
And if we become parents someday, I want us to raise our children by example.
I genuinely think we'd make an amazing team as parents.
There's one thing I really want to experience with you.
A proper trip.
Not one afternoon. Not one date.
Four or five days.
Just you and me.
No rushing back.
No metro goodbyes.
Just being somewhere together.
And I know what I want our home to feel like.
I don't need it to be perfect.
I want it to feel like a warm bowl of soup on a terrible day.
A place we want to come back to when life has exhausted us.
A place where we can put everything outside the door for a while.
Our resting place.
Our safe space.
Our home.
And when we're old, I hope one thing never changes.
The romance.
I hope we still look at each other and feel that same little spark.
I promise I'll stick by you.
And if I get to grow old with you, I hope I live long enough to spend all those years happily in your arms.

chapter_9.title: THE THINGS I'LL NEVER LET YOU FORGET
content: Okay. Enough emotional nonsense.
Now let me tell you the things I will NEVER let you forget.
I still remember you saying, 'আজ এর বেশি এগুলো উচিত না.'
You absolutely cringe whenever I bring it up.
Which is exactly why I am putting it in this movie.
And then there's your greatest crime.
How can you stay without calling me?
How can you not text me?
How are you so calm?
How do you not miss me?
How are you not going crazy for me?
Honestly, I don't understand you.
You are also unbelievably good at cooking.
And yet you keep insisting that you cook only 'okay-okay'.
Please stop.
We both know that's not true.
Another thing you do is smile whenever I say something.
And sometimes I genuinely want to ask, 'WHY ARE YOU SMILING?'
But secretly, I'd miss that smile if you stopped.
I love how strongly you stand by what you believe in.
Although sometimes I think you could relax just a little.
The world is changing, Babu.
And you don't have to like everyone to live alongside them.
But that's also part of loving you.
I can admire you and still disagree with you.
And of course, there is your greatest achievement.
GREEN CHUTNEY CHAMPION.
Babu.
Babai.
Whatever I call you, you're still the same person I somehow chose to love.
And you are lucky I love you.
Because you will never get someone like me.

chapter_10.title: FOR YOU
content: If you were sitting directly in front of me right now, the first thing I would say is thank you.
Thank you to God for bringing you into my life.
You have always felt like God's greatest gift to me.
Thank you for loving me unconditionally.
Thank you for everything.
And I'm sorry.
I'm sorry for the times I misunderstood you.
For the times I rushed to conclusions.
For the times I didn't stop to understand your perspective.
Four years together have taught me that two people can be completely different.
What feels okay to one person might not feel okay to the other.
And sometimes loving each other means finding that middle ground.
Something I've never properly told you is how much I just want to hold your hand and stay with you for my whole life.
At IIT Bombay, there is so much around me.
But you're not here.
And sometimes a city without you feels like an empty city to me.
I love you very, very deeply.
And whenever you doubt yourself, I want you to remember this.
Look at the Paris Tower.
Look at the appreciation gift I sent you.
Look at the photograph I gave you.
Those things are reminders that you are special in someone's life.
No matter how many hardships you face.
No matter how many people make you feel like a failure.
There will always be one woman, sitting very far away, believing in you.
Praying for you.
Waiting for you.
And seeing you as her champion.
You are loved.
You are valued.
You are enough.
And Shayok, if there is one thing I want you to know before this movie ends...
I love you.
